subject: Competitive bake-off recap & proposed next steps (Acme Analytics)
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwoodinference.com>
To: Jared Cole <jared@acmeanalytics.com>, Michelle Tan <michelle.tan@acmeanalytics.com>
Cc: Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie_nguyen@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Wed, 4 Mar 2026 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: Competitive bake-off recap & proposed next steps (Acme Analytics)

Hi Jared / Michelle —

Thanks for the time this morning. Quick recap from our call and proposed next steps so we all have the same plan for the bake-off.

Key pain points you reiterated:
- High inference latency on current vendor (p95 often > 600ms) impacting user experience for interactive flows.
- Unit cost for embeddings/generation is higher than expected — goal is to reduce cost per active user by at least 30%.
- Limited observability (no token-level cost breakdown or request-level tracing) which makes regressions hard to diagnose.
- Security/compliance: need SOC 2 evidence and EU data residency for some workloads.

Goals for the bake-off / decision criteria we captured:
1) Latency: p95 < 200ms for standard 512-token generation workload (1k concurrent sessions target).
2) Quality: embeddings similarity A/B on your 5k-doc retrieval test set (we'll provide eval script).
3) Cost: 6-month run-rate for projected traffic — goal is at least 25–30% savings vs current vendor.
4) Operability: tracing, per-route dashboards, and audit logs accessible to your security team.
5) Support & SLA: dedicated escalation path and predictable capacity (reserved option).

Competitive notes (from our side):
- Redwood: unified runtime, intelligent batching + KV caching, predictable dedicated capacity options. We think we can hit the latency and cost targets with the recommended config.
- CompetitorX: strong latency on short sequences but limited caching/observability tooling; pricing tends to spike under sustained concurrency.
- CloudVendorY: integrated with your infra but has higher egress and per-token costs in our estimates.

Open questions for your team:
- Can you confirm the 5k doc eval dataset and share the retrieval script?
- Which region(s) must we guarantee data residency for (EU only or both EU + US)?
- Do you require SOC 2 Type II before any PoC infra is provisioned?

Proposed technical tests (we recommend the following order):
A) Latency/load test: 1k concurrent sessions, 512-token baseline generation, p95 target < 200ms.
B) Embeddings quality A/B: run your 5k-doc retrieval evaluation, report MRR and recall@10.
C) Cost projection: run a simulated 30-day traffic profile and provide a 6-month run-rate estimate.

Next steps (action items):
- Action (Marissa / Redwood): attach slide deck + test plan (attached). Rishi will run the latency/load test and share results within 3 business days once we have dataset and access.
- Action (Acme): share dataset, retrieval script, and confirm required regions + SOC 2 requirement.
- Schedule: propose a 60-min technical deep dive next Tuesday 3/10 — please confirm availability.

Attachments: redwood-bakeoff-slide-deck.pdf (overview + config recommendations), acme-bakeoff-test-plan.xlsx (detailed steps & expected outputs).

Thanks — looking forward to running the tests.

Best,
Marissa Cole
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
marissa_cole@redwoodinference.com
(415) 555-0123

From: Jared Cole <jared@acmeanalytics.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Michelle Tan <michelle.tan@acmeanalytics.com>
Date: Wed, 4 Mar 2026 10:03:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Competitive bake-off recap & proposed next steps (Acme Analytics)

Thanks Marissa — this is helpful and aligns with how we walked through things internally. A few clarifications from our side: 

1) Dataset: we'll hand over the 5k-doc eval set and the retrieval script by EOD Thursday (3/5).
2) Regions: EU residency is required for our EU customer subset; US residency is OK for our internal analytics workloads. Ideally we'd like EU-only for the production pipeline.
3) SOC2: we require SOC 2 Type II evidence before signing off on any production-level contracts; for the PoC infra we can do a limited test environment under NDA but we'd still need relevant security docs.

Questions / asks: 
- Can you provide a simple side-by-side price comparison (redwood vs CompetitorX vs CloudVendorY) assuming our projected traffic (attached sheet would be ideal)?
- For the latency test, can you confirm whether the 1k concurrency test will run from EU region endpoints? We want results that reflect EU latencies.

Timeline: we'd like to conclude the bake-off in 3 weeks (target decision by 3/25). The technical deep dive next week on 3/10 works for us — Jared and Michelle are available 10:00–12:00 PT.

Appreciate the clear plan — looping in our security lead (mike.s@acmeanalytics.com) separately.

Best,
Jared
Director of Product, Acme Analytics
Jared@acmeanalytics.com

From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwoodinference.com>

Jared — thanks for the quick reply and for the timeline. Answering inline and confirming next steps: 

> Dataset: we'll hand over the 5k-doc eval set and the retrieval script by EOD Thursday (3/5).
We'll’ll watch for that. Rishi will pick up the files and provision the EU test endpoints as soon as we have them.

> Regions: EU residency is required for our EU customer subset; US residency is OK for our internal analytics workloads.
We can provision EU-only test endpoints for the production-like run. Rishi — can you confirm estimated lead time to spin up the EU reserved pool for the load test (expected 1–2 days once dataset and creds are available)?

> SOC2: we require SOC 2 Type II evidence before signing off on any production-level contracts; for the PoC infra we can do a limited test environment under NDA but we'd still need relevant security docs.
Understood. Attaching our SOC 2 summary and a redacted evidence package (we'll send full Type II on request through your security portal). For the PoC we can run under NDA; I'll have our compliance team prepare an access checklist.

Price comparison / cost model: I'll attach a one-sheet price comparison and populate the projected traffic numbers into your template if you can share it.

Technical deep-dive: 3/10 at 10:30 PT works for our team. I've penciled it in and will send a calendar invite once you confirm. Rishi will present the test results and walk through the config.

Action items (updated):
- Marissa: send SOC 2 summary + slide deck + initial price comparison (attached).
- Rishi: provision EU test endpoints and run latency/load test after dataset delivered. Estimate provisioning 24–48 hours.
- Acme: share dataset + retrieval script + any access constraints (EOD 3/5).
- Schedule: confirm 3/10 10:30 PT for technical deep-dive and I'll send invite.

Attachments included: redwood-bakeoff-slide-deck.pdf, acme-bakeoff-test-plan.xlsx, redwood-soc2-summary.pdf

If that all looks good I'll send the calendar invite and the test plan and Rishi will get started as soon as we have the files.

Thanks — excited to run this.

Best,
Marissa Cole
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
marissa_cole@redwoodinference.com
